syntaxNeeds.ordinary-join-semi: Doris requires LEFT SEMI JOIN, not bare SEMI JOIN. joinType explicitly lists LEFT SEMI and RIGHT SEMI. The unchanged case is still useful as editor input, but its DuckDB syntax is not an executable Doris query.
syntaxNeeds.ordinary-join-anti: Doris requires LEFT ANTI JOIN, not bare ANTI JOIN. joinType explicitly lists LEFT ANTI and RIGHT ANTI. The unchanged case is still useful as editor input, but its DuckDB syntax is not an executable Doris query.

priority.join-ambiguous: Ordinary native resolution chooses src.id for an unqualified id shared by two joined inputs. The supplied engine witness independently rejects the ambiguity. Fix this native/analyzer disagreement before introducing another ordinary-SQL analyzer.
priority.ordinary-group-alias: Native resolution finds the SELECT alias kind but does not retain the passthrough Kotlin navigation target. GROUP BY alias visibility is also registered by DorisAliasResolveExtension. This is an ordinary native binding/metadata disagreement, not unsupported Doris syntax.
priority.ordinary-join-right-semi: RIGHT SEMI is valid Doris grammar, unlike DuckDB's native witness syntax. Doris's native SqlTableType/resolver fails to expose the preserved right input. The native syntax witness in the report confirms grammar acceptance.
priority.ordinary-join-right-anti: RIGHT ANTI is valid Doris grammar, unlike DuckDB's native witness syntax. Doris's native SqlTableType/resolver fails to expose the preserved right input. The native syntax witness in the report confirms grammar acceptance.
priority.ordinary-join-right: The nullable side of an outer join cannot retain a non-null Kotlin input guarantee. Native scopes and completion currently retain NON_NULL/Long/Int; the supplied independent outer-join witness proves unmatched rows exist.
priority.ordinary-join-full: Both sides of a FULL JOIN can be unmatched. Native scopes and completion currently retain NON_NULL/Long/Int from the input declarations. The native syntax witness accepts FULL JOIN.
priority.pipe-star-join: The v2.1 source case no longer probes the old extra stageScopeAt axis. Its reference, resolve, navigation and completion axes now match. Scope still lacks the identity, knowledge and navigation data required by the result contract, and PIPE relation-level diagnostics are unavailable.
priority.physical-pipe: Real SQL-file DDL models are also registered as same-id offline local data sources. PIPE still lacks native reference/navigation PSI and the scope display cannot attribute physical SQL types, identity or completeness.
priority.self-join-same-slot: Native ordinary-SQL resolution binds an unqualified id shared by two aliases of the same slot. The aliases are distinct relations even though their declaration pointers are identical; ambiguity must not be resolved by shared navigation identity.
priority.left-using-merged-star: Native USING output retains the nullable right-side code declaration as non-null in scope/completion. The Brikk navigation handler also loses passthrough navigation for the merged id; native XML navigation targets retain it.
priority.set-nullability-names-union-all: Native set-output references bind the left Kotlin declaration instead of computed output identity. Visible scope/order and completion do not implement the output column order and nullable result contract.
priority.union-unanimous-origin: Even unanimously sourced UNION output has incomplete native output scope, order and completion. Reference/navigation acceptance is checked separately and is not inferred from visible completion names.
priority.unknown-table: The native hook resolves an id under an unresolved table to a synthetic computed column. A closed catalog should report the table, not bind a fabricated column or add a second missing-column diagnostic.
priority.unknown-table-open-catalog: Without a closed catalog, table existence is unknown. Native resolution still fabricates a computed id and reports table/column errors instead of preserving that uncertainty.

expectationReview: The four shared files cases.jsonl, facts.json, witnesses.json and duckdb-disagreements.json are copied verbatim from DuckDB 13ad2d5, corpus v2.2. Only 159 of the 177 cases are tagged for Doris; non-applicable cases do not run.

Doris exposes no PIPE knowledge, identity or navigation targets through pipeScope/pipeDisplay. Those values stay null; scope/order observations do not invent provenance from matching names. These differences include API representation gaps, not only wrong inventories.

The ordinary references and resolve axes both observe native resolution because Doris has no separate ordinary-SQL relation analyzer. DuckDB's references axis observes its analyzer while resolve observes the native hook. Cross-product reference differences must retain that distinction.

DuckDB diagnostics come from its relation-contract annotator; Doris has no equivalent partial-contract/PIPE diagnostic annotator. Doris diagnostics here come from the real SqlResolveInspection visitor after DorisHighlightInfoFilter, so generic errors in non-slot negative cases are not Kotlin contract claims.

Set-output expectations deliberately forbid unique Kotlin origin/navigation. The native resolver's left-output declaration navigation is a policy disagreement with that rule, not evidence of incorrect set rows or SQL column naming. Native query/set-operation grammar and DuckDB's independent engine witnesses agree on the output names.

The corpus intentionally contains incomplete and non-slot calls. Native syntax refusals are recorded without rewriting shared SQL or offsets. Double-quoted aliases and NATURAL JOIN are not accepted by the pinned Doris grammar. Argument-bearing and qualified src calls are not relation slots.

The 34 Doris engine witnesses are parsed against the bundled FE grammar. Only the NATURAL JOIN witness needs a separate explicit-join/projection correction. LEFT SEMI/ANTI witnesses are accepted. Syntax is verified, but rows and semantic rejection are not: no server runs and the copied verified:false flags remain unchanged.

V2.2 removes the double-quoted alias case from Doris, adds all four FULL USING nullability combinations, multipart physical table identities, declaration ranges and execution probes, and corrects GROUP BY visibility and anonymous LIMIT/OFFSET/DISTINCT boundary expectations. Computed SQL types are no longer inferred from Kotlin display types.

All three declaration-range probes match native SQL PSI. The multipart physical-table reference, resolve, navigation and completion axes identify two.t correctly, but SqlTableType does not expose that fully qualified scope at the caret.

FULL USING merged-id facts must be computed with no unique Kotlin declaration. Native scope/resolution instead retains an input identity and loses the specified nullable result metadata; all five binding/display axes are explicit known differences for each nullability combination.

Execution probes substitute only the corpus engineRelations slots, lower with core and parse the generated SQL with the pinned FE grammar. Output columns are observed from core outputShape. No Doris server is run, so rows remain null and the seven coreExecution differences are unverified row results, not claimed execution failures.

Native declarations use foreign XML text targets so SQL column declarations cannot override the contract's names or introduce artificial INT types. Brikk declarations are Kotlin PSI. Known navigation-only differences are listed by lane; neither lane substitutes a new ordinary-SQL analyzer.

Known differences are explicit case/axis lists. Unlisted changes fail. A listed axis that becomes equal also fails until its stale flag is removed, so fixed behavior returns to the green corpus. Corpus reports are compared byte-for-byte across two independent runs per lane.
